content:
client_acme: Hi, we're seeing repeated issues with SSE streaming when our client rotates tokens mid-stream. The stream disconnects with a 429 and on reconnect the new token is charged for the remaining tokens AND the original token gets billed for the part it already streamed. End result: duplicate token accounting + the client only got a partial completion. Repro included below.

sofia_support: Sorry about that — can you paste the minimal repro (curl or client code) and a request id or log snippet? Also which SDK/version?

client_acme: Here's a minimal curl repro. We intentionally rotate token after ~3s to simulate refresh.

client_acme: ```bash
curl -N 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer TOKEN_A" 
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" 
  "https://api.redwood.inference/v1/stream?model=xlarge" 
  |
  ( sleep 3; export TOKEN=TOKEN_B; # client refresh logic replaces header and reconnects )
```

client_acme: Server side logs for request r-reqid-01:
```
[2024-07-10T15:00:01Z] auth: token=TOKEN_A req=r-reqid-01 allow
[2024-07-10T15:00:02Z] stream: emit chunk id=1 tokens=120 req=r-reqid-01
[2024-07-10T15:00:03Z] auth: token expired mid-stream -> respond 429 req=r-reqid-01
[2024-07-10T15:00:03Z] accounting: flush consumed=120 token=TOKEN_A session=r-reqid-01
[2024-07-10T15:00:04Z] client: reconnect with TOKEN_B new-conn-id=r-reqid-01-reconn1
[2024-07-10T15:00:04Z] auth: token=TOKEN_B req=r-reqid-01-reconn1 allow
[2024-07-10T15:00:04Z] stream: resume emit chunk id=2 tokens=80 req=r-reqid-01-reconn1
[2024-07-10T15:00:05Z] accounting: flush consumed=80 token=TOKEN_B session=r-reqid-01-reconn1
```

client_acme: On our billing dashboard both TOKEN_A and TOKEN_B show charges for the same overall request, and the output we received only had chunks 1 and 2 but the model log shows a single completion.

sofia_support: Thanks — that log is super helpful. @marta_engineering can you take a look? Looks like accounting flushed at 429 and then the reconnect created a separate accounting entry for the continuation. We should be attributing the whole logical session to a single token or session id to avoid double billing.

marta_engineering: I see. From the runtime perspective, SSE sessions are treated as independent HTTP connections. When a 429 is emitted, middleware currently flushes the per-connection token usage immediately. If the client reconnects with a different token, accounting currently attributes the subsequent usage to the new token. That produces two separate accounting entries for what the app considers a single logical request.

marta_engineering: Quick triage: we need to decide whether to (A) always attribute the entire logical session to the first token seen for that request id, or (B) implement a session handshake token that persists across reconnects and is used for accounting. Option A is simpler but could be exploited if a token is stolen. Option B is safer but needs protocol/SDK changes.

ajay_oncall: Repro locally with the exact flow — confirmed duplicate accounting. Found race: accounting flush happens in auth middleware when response code >= 400, before the runtime has a chance to mark the session as resumable.

ajay_oncall: Relevant snippet from middleware:```go
if resp.StatusCode >= 400 {
  accounting.flush(connID)
}
```

ajay_oncall: If we move the flush to the runtime's session-complete hook (only for resumable streams), we can avoid double counting. Patch prototype works in local tests.

olivia_billing: For the customer facing side, we'll need to refund the duplicated tokens and update billing attribution. Can you DM the full list of affected tokens and amounts? We'll also want a short customer note explaining root cause and mitigation plan.

sofia_support: @client_acme we'll coordinate refunds. Can you confirm how many request ids in your tenant were affected and approximate timeframe?

client_acme: We saw ~12 incidents over the last 2 days, all between 2024-07-09 22:00 UTC and 2024-07-11 03:00 UTC. I can list req ids tomorrow morning. We want a fix though — these duplicates hurt our quota.

marta_engineering: Action plan: (1) temporary workaround: server to prefer attributing mid-stream reconnects to the original token if reconnect contains header `X-Resume-Session: r-reqid-01` and the original token is still valid. We'll roll a config flag for this to limit blast radius. (2) medium: move accounting flush out of immediate error-path and into session lifecycle hooks. (3) long: implement session-level auth token that survives refresh (session token) with SDK updates.

marta_engineering: Patch for (1) ready for staging; scheduling deploy to staging at 2024-07-11T02:00 UTC. Requesting quick QA from support.

sofia_support: I'll validate with client after staging deploy. Olivia, please prepare refund batch once we confirm the affected token list.

olivia_billing: Roger. I'll prepare a provisional credit for the tenant and hold until we confirm exact amounts.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: staging cluster -> service=streaming-runtime image=streaming-runtime:v2.14.7-patch account-resume-fix

ajay_oncall: Quick note — edge case where the client reconnects with a brand new request id (no resume header) and different token: we can't retroactively attribute, so those will still show as separate charges. Encourage clients to use resume header for reconnects. We'll add guidance to docs.

client_acme: Good call, we'll update our client to send X-Resume-Session on reconnects. Thanks for fast turnaround.

sofia_support: Closing loop: staging deploy is running, QA passed for resume header flows, scheduling prod deploy tentatively 2024-07-11T05:00 UTC. I'll post updates here once prod deploy completes and when billing credits are issued. :thumbsup:

client_acme: Thanks everyone — appreciate the help.
